message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: 'Link Checker'

# **What it does**: Renders the content of every page and check all internal links.
# **Why we have it**: To make sure all links connect correctly.
# **Who does it impact**: Docs content.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    # branches: [master, 'release/**']
    paths:
      - '**/*.md'
      - '**/link-check.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [2023.x, 2025.0.x, 2025.1.x, "release/**"]
    paths:
      - '**/*.md'
      - '**/link-check.yml'

permissions:
  contents: read
  # Needed for the 'trilom/file-changes-action' action
  pull-requests: read

# This allows a subsequently queued workflow run to interrupt previous runs
concurrency:
  group: '${{ github.workflow }} @ ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.label || github.head_ref || github.ref }}'
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  check-links:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Get script
        run: |
          wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xuruidong/markdown-link-checker/main/link_checker.py

      - name: Setup python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: '3.9'

      - name: Link check (critical, all files)
        run: |
          # python link_checker.py ./ --enable-external --ignore "http://apisix.iresty.com" "https://www.upyun.com" "https://github.com/apache/apisix/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg" "https://httpbin.org/" "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cache"
          python link_checker.py ./",
  "rationale": "The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern (bound jobs with a custom timeout) is supported by the pattern record and a measured fork experiment showing a custom job timeout reduces runaway consumption (26.82% elapsed savings in the experiment). Its precondition—representative successful-duration history—is met by this repository's CI history, which shows five successful link-check runs of roughly 16–19 seconds each. The contraindication (valid slow runs exceeding the limit) is not triggered because a 5-minute budget gives roughly 15x headroom over observed successful runs. The change is minimal: adding `timeout-minutes: 5` to the single `check-links` job. It preserves all triggers, paths, permissions, concurrency cancellation, steps, and test coverage, and adds no privileged actions, secrets, publishing/deployment operations, or new network access.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508"]
}
